finding: A submitted cookie set/remove could succeed while late revocation made the caller see failure.
resolution: Keep authorization and optional permission checks before native mutation dispatch.
Treat dispatch as acceptance and preserve the native success/error after revocation.
Discard revoked reads and reject subsequent calls.
Keep the two-second deadline independent of revocation; after submission report an unknown outcome.
Retain admission slots until native settlement, without retries or rollback.

focused.regressionBefore: All eight set/delete cases reproduced incorrect failure reporting before the fix.
coverage: Permission loss, scope exit, pagehide and native connection revocation

reviews: Trust and data delivery: pre-dispatch authorization and late-read checks retained; writes return no cookie data.
Simplification and resource lifecycle: reuse existing admission slots and controller; deadline settles independently of revocation.
Consumers and verification: wrapper callbacks, documented outcomes, final scoped diff and native package hashes checked.
limitations: Delayed native responses are deterministically injected in unit tests; real browsers verify ordinary native cookie operations and scope/permission revocation.
A submitted browser write cannot be cancelled; page teardown can make its result undeliverable.
Optional clipboard, notification and download desktop suites were not rerun.
Offline fixtures do not establish live-site coverage.
